newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher on light volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher on light volumes.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Monday, but volumes were very light, with activity limited by the Passover holiday this week as well as an Islamic holiday, traders said.
"We expect nearby gold futures will oscillate mostly within a $335 to $375 an ounce trading range for the remainder of the year," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
COMEX June gold settled up $1.50 an ounce at $344.90, after trading a $342.90-345.10 range. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was only 5,000 lots.

Open interest in COMEX gold was little changed Friday at 163,974 contracts, after recovering slightly from 12 month lows last week as some new short positions were established by funds in the wake of last week's lower-than-expected U.S. inflation data.

But since then daily momentum oscillators have begun to recover again, and volatility measures have continued to subside, as gold quickly found support just below $340 an ounce, not far from the four year lows seen in January.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $342.70/10 compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $342.20 and the New York close Friday around $341.10/60.
"Interest rates and the U.S. dollar appear to be the present fundamental focus for the gold market," Rinehimer said.

"Gold prices are expected to reflect prospects for another tightening move by the Federal Reserve at the May 20 FOMC meeting, following its move in March to increase the fed funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 percent."

"Assuming the markets feel comfortable that the Fed actions will sustain a relatively low inflation environment, then future tightening moves are likely to prove negative for gold prices by keeping inflationary expectations low and increasing the cost of holding gold."
But other analysts note that in inflation adjusted terms the gold price is now the same as the historic low of $103 an ounce seen in 1976.
COMEX May silver ended up 2.2 cents at $4.735 an ounce, after trading a narrow $4.720-$4.755 range. Estimated total COMEX silver volume was 22,000 contracts.
Silver prices have also changed little in the past few days, after finding support around $4.70 in the bullion market last week, following a slide to two month lows.
Rising interest rates, a strong dollar and weak investor demand are capping any rise in silver prices, but industrial demand remains robust in the U.S. and Japan, analysts said.
NYMEX July platinum gained $3.30 an ounce to $380.50, the highest close since mid-March, while the July/October contango narrowed further to 60 cents from around $2.50 in early April.
The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread climbed to a contract high at $32.40 an ounce.
NYMEX June palladium gained $1.15 at $155.75.
Other platinum group metal prices have gained along with platinum and palladium, since the disruption to Russian supplies last December.
Rhodium, was quoted around $260 an ounce Monday, up from a multi-year low around $190 two months ago.

"The situation remains unclear with regard to Russian intentions for marketing PGMs, but the key is likely to be (Russian Finance Minister) Chubais's comments last week that they are looking at new approaches to raising revenue," Johnson Matthey precious metals marketing manager, Jeremy Coombes said.

"The question of which Russian ministry is likely to be in charge should be resolved soon, but in the meantime liquidity remains low in the physical PGM market in Zurich keeping lease rates high and prices firm for both platinum and palladium," he said.
